The Method of ℳn{\cal M}_{n}-Extension: The KdV EquationThanks: aslipekcan@hacettepe.edu.tr

Metin Gürses ††thanks: gurses@fen.bilkent.edu.tr Affiliation: Department of Mathematics, Faculty of Science Affiliation: Bilkent University, 06800 Ankara - Turkey Affiliation: Aslı Pekcan Affiliation: Department of Mathematics, Faculty of Science Affiliation: Hacettepe University, 06800 Ankara - Turkey
Abstract

In this work we generalize ℳ2{\cal M}_{2}-extension that has been introduced recently. For illustration we use the KdV equation. We present five different ℳ3{\cal M}_{3}-extensions of the KdV equation and their recursion operators. We give a compact form of ℳn{\cal M}_{n}-extension of the KdV equation and recursion operator of the coupled KdV system. The method of ℳn{\cal M}_{n}-extension can be applied to any integrable scalar equation to obtain integrable multi-field system of equations. We also present unshifted and shifted nonlocal reductions of an example of ℳ3{\cal M}_{3}-extension of KdV.

Keywords. ℳn{\cal M}_{n}-extension, Coupled systems, Recursion operator, Integrability, Nonlocal reductions.

1 Introduction

Obtaining new integrable systems is a very important topic in nonlinear science due to their rich structure. One of the methods to get an integrable system is using the Lax representations in algebras of higher rank. Another method is using perturbation technique preserving integrability [1]. In [2] we introduced a new method that we call ℳ2{\cal M}_{2}-extension. Particularly, we considered the extensions of fifth order integrable Sawada-Kotera (SK) and Kaup-Kupershmidt (KK) equations. This method can be used to any integrable scalar equation to obtain integrable systems. Besides obtaining an integrable system we can also derive Hirota bilinear form and recursion operator of the obtained system by extending Hirota bilinear form and recursion operator of the scalar equation.

In this work we generalize ℳ2{\cal M}_{2}-extension [2] to ℳn{\cal M}_{n}-extension. We use ℳn{\cal M}_{n}-extension method on integrable scalar equations to obtain systems of integrable equations and new integrable nonlocal equations. As an illustration, here we consider Korteweg-de Vries (KdV) equation [3]. Our work on the ℳn{\cal M}_{n}-extension of modified KdV equation is also in progress [4]. Note that multi-field extension of the KdV equation had also been studied in [5]-[8].

The ℳn{\cal M}_{n}-extension method consists of three main steps. The first step is to replace the dynamical variable of the integrable scalar equation by u→u0​Σ0+u1​Σ1+u2​Σ2+⋯+un−1​Σn−1u\to u^{0}\,\Sigma_{0}+u^{1}\Sigma_{1}+u^{2}\,\Sigma_{2}+\cdots+u^{n-1}\,\Sigma_{n-1} where u0=uu^{0}=u, ui,(i=1,2⋯,n−1)u^{i},(i=1,2\cdots,n-1) are the dynamical variables of the system. Here, the basis Σi\Sigma_{i}, (i=0,1,2,⋯,n−1)(i=0,1,2,\cdots,n-1) of the ℳn{\cal M}_{n} algebra satisfies the following multiplication rule:

Σj⋅Σi=Σi⋅Σj=fi​jk​Σk,\Sigma_{j}\cdot\Sigma_{i}=\Sigma_{i}\cdot\Sigma_{j}=f^{k}_{ij}\,\Sigma_{k}, (1.1)

where we use summation convention for the repeated indices and fi​jkf^{k}_{ij} are the structural constants of the algebra which are symmetrical with respect to the indices ii and jj, i.e., fi​jk=fj​ikf^{k}_{ij}=f^{k}_{ji}. We obtain a system of equations for the dynamical variables uiu^{i}, its recursion operator and Lax pair. It is natural that these operators contain the structural constants fi​jkf^{k}_{ij} of the algebra. Second step is to obtain the symmetrical version of the system by defining new dynamical variables q1=u+u1+u2+⋯+un−1q_{1}=u+u^{1}+u^{2}+\cdots+u^{n-1}, q2=u−u1+u2+⋯+un−1q_{2}=u-u^{1}+u^{2}+\cdots+u^{n-1}, ⋯\cdots, qn=u+u1+u2+⋯−un−1q_{n}=u+u^{1}+u^{2}+\cdots-u^{n-1}. At the same time one can obtain the recursion operator with respect to the dynamical variables qiq_{i}. The third step is to apply consistent reductions to obtain standard (unshifted) nonlocal and shifted nonlocal reductions of the systems for qiq_{i} [4], [9]-[22]. All these equations are new and integrable. Using the reduction formulas, one can obtain the recursion operators of the nonlocal differential equations. Soliton solutions of the standard nonlocal and shifted nonlocal equations can be easily obtained by using soliton solutions of the systems and reduction formulas.

2 ℳ2{\cal M}_{2}-extension of the KdV equation

Let u→U=u​I+v​Σu\to U=uI+v\Sigma where Σ2=α​I+β​Σ\Sigma^{2}=\alpha I+\beta\,\Sigma for α=−det⁡(Σ)\alpha=-\mathrm{det}(\Sigma) and β=tr⁡(Σ)\beta=\mathrm{tr}(\Sigma). Hence using

Ut=Ux​x​x+6​U​Ux,U_{t}=U_{xxx}+6UU_{x}, (2.1)

the ℳ2{\cal M}_{2}-extension of the KdV equation gives [23]-[25]

ut=ux​x​x+6​u​ux+6​α​v​vx,\displaystyle u_{t}=u_{xxx}+6uu_{x}+6\alpha vv_{x}, (2.2)
vt=vx​x​x+6​(u​v)x+6​β​v​vx.\displaystyle v_{t}=v_{xxx}+6(uv)_{x}+6\beta\,vv_{x}. (2.3)

The case when α=β=0\alpha=\beta=0 gives first order perturbation equation of KdV [26]. Choosing

Σ=(0α1β)\Sigma=\left(\begin{array}[]{ll}0&\alpha\cr 1&\beta\cr\end{array}\right) (2.4)

we obtain

ℛ=(RK​d​Vα⁡(4​v+2​vx​D−1)4​v+2​vx​D−1RK​d​V+β⁡(4​v+2​vx​D−1)).{\cal R}=\left(\begin{array}[]{ll}R_{KdV}&\quad\quad\quad\alpha(4v+2v_{x}\,D^{-1})\cr 4v+2v_{x}\,D^{-1}&\quad\quad R_{KdV}+\beta(4v+2v_{x}\,D^{-1})\cr\end{array}\right). (2.5)

The Lax pair of the above system is given by

L=I​D2+u​I+v​Σ,\displaystyle L=ID^{2}+uI+v\Sigma, (2.6)
𝒜=4​I​D3+(6​u​D+3​ux)​I+(6​v​D+3​vx)​Σ.\displaystyle{\cal A}=4ID^{3}+(6uD+3u_{x})I+(6vD+3v_{x})\Sigma. (2.7)

Remark 1: The algebra in this ℳ2{\cal M}_{2}-extension of the KdV equation is the unification of the algebras in the ℳ2{\cal M}_{2}-extensions in [2], [4].

Remark 2: The functions uu and vv satisfying the system of equations (2.2) and (2.3) are both linear combinations of two different solutions p=u+a​vp=u+av and q=u−a​vq=u-av of KdV equations pt=px​x​x+6​p​pxp_{t}=p_{xxx}+6pp_{x} and qt=qx​x​x+6​q​qxq_{t}=q_{xxx}+6qq_{x} if α=1+β\alpha=1+\beta.

3 ℳ3{\cal M}_{3}-extension of the KdV equation

For application we use again the KdV equation. Let u→U=u0​Σ0+u1​Σ1+u2​Σ2u\to U=u^{0}\,\Sigma_{0}+u^{1}\Sigma_{1}+u^{2}\Sigma_{2} where Σ0=I\Sigma_{0}=I and Σ1\Sigma_{1} and Σ2\Sigma_{2} satisfy the following five different choices of the ℳ3{\cal M}_{3} algebra:

I. Σ12=0,Σ22=0,Σ1⋅Σ2=Σ2⋅Σ1=0,\Sigma_{1}^{2}=0,~\Sigma_{2}^{2}=0,~\Sigma_{1}\cdot\Sigma_{2}=\Sigma_{2}\cdot\Sigma_{1}=0,

II. Σ12=Σ2,Σ22=0,Σ1⋅Σ2=Σ2⋅Σ1=0,\Sigma_{1}^{2}=\Sigma_{2},~\Sigma_{2}^{2}=0,~\Sigma_{1}\cdot\Sigma_{2}=\Sigma_{2}\cdot\Sigma_{1}=0,

III. Σ12=Σ1,Σ22=0,Σ1⋅Σ2=Σ2⋅Σ1=0,\Sigma_{1}^{2}=\Sigma_{1},~\Sigma_{2}^{2}=0,~\Sigma_{1}\cdot\Sigma_{2}=\Sigma_{2}\cdot\Sigma_{1}=0,

IV. Σ12=Σ1,Σ22=Σ2,Σ1⋅Σ2=Σ2⋅Σ1=0,\Sigma_{1}^{2}=\Sigma_{1},~\Sigma_{2}^{2}=\Sigma_{2},~\Sigma_{1}\cdot\Sigma_{2}=\Sigma_{2}\cdot\Sigma_{1}=0,

V. Σ12=Σ1,Σ22=0,Σ1⋅Σ2=Σ2⋅Σ1=Σ2.\Sigma_{1}^{2}=\Sigma_{1},~\Sigma_{2}^{2}=0,~\Sigma_{1}\cdot\Sigma_{2}=\Sigma_{2}\cdot\Sigma_{1}=\Sigma_{2}.

Here we can also write the matrix forms of the basis members Σ1\Sigma_{1} and Σ2\Sigma_{2}, explicitly. For instance, we have

Σ1=(000000010),Σ2=(010000000)\Sigma_{1}=\left(\begin{array}[]{lll}0&0&0\cr 0&0&0\cr 0&1&0\end{array}\right),\quad\Sigma_{2}=\left(\begin{array}[]{lll}0&1&0\cr 0&0&0\cr 0&0&0\end{array}\right) (3.1)

for the Case I.

The method of ℳ3{\cal M}_{3}-extension gives the following systems of KdV equations and their recursion operators corresponding to the above Cases I-V. We let u0=uu^{0}=u , u1=vu^{1}=v, and u2=wu^{2}=w. We have

I. ut=ux​x​x+6​u​uxu_{t}=u_{xxx}+6uu_{x}, vt=vx​x​x+6​(u​v)xv_{t}=v_{xxx}+6(uv)_{x}, wt=wx​x​x+6​(u​w)xw_{t}=w_{xxx}+6(uw)_{x}, and

ℛ=(RK​d​V004​v+2​vx​D−1RK​d​V04​w+2​wx​D−10RK​d​V),{\cal R}=\left(\begin{array}[]{lll}R_{KdV}&\quad\quad 0&\quad\quad 0\cr 4v+2v_{x}\,D^{-1}&\quad R_{KdV}&\quad\quad 0\cr 4w+2w_{x}\,D^{-1}&\quad\quad 0&\quad R_{KdV}\cr\end{array}\right), (3.2)

II. ut=ux​x​x+6​u​uxu_{t}=u_{xxx}+6uu_{x}, vt=vx​x​x+6​(u​v)xv_{t}=v_{xxx}+6(uv)_{x}, wt=wx​x​x+6​(u​w)x+6​v​vxw_{t}=w_{xxx}+6(uw)_{x}+6vv_{x}, and

ℛ=(RK​d​V004​v+2​vx​D−1RK​d​V04​w+2​wx​D−14​v+2​vx​D−1RK​d​V),{\cal R}=\left(\begin{array}[]{lll}R_{KdV}&\quad\quad 0&\quad\quad 0\cr 4v+2v_{x}\,D^{-1}&\quad R_{KdV}&\quad\quad 0\cr 4w+2w_{x}\,D^{-1}&\quad 4v+2v_{x}\,D^{-1}&\quad R_{KdV}\cr\end{array}\right), (3.3)

III. ut=ux​x​x+6​u​uxu_{t}=u_{xxx}+6uu_{x}, vt=vx​x​x+6​(u​v)x+6​v​vxv_{t}=v_{xxx}+6(uv)_{x}+6vv_{x}, wt=wx​x​x+6​(u​w)xw_{t}=w_{xxx}+6(uw)_{x}, and

ℛ=(RK​d​V004​v+2​vx​D−1RK​d​V+4​v+2​vx​D−104​w+2​wx​D−10RK​d​V),{\cal R}=\left(\begin{array}[]{lll}R_{KdV}&\quad\quad\quad 0&\quad\quad\quad 0\cr 4v+2v_{x}\,D^{-1}&\quad R_{KdV}+4v+2v_{x}\,D^{-1}&\quad\quad\quad 0\cr 4w+2w_{x}\,D^{-1}&\quad\quad\quad 0&\quad R_{KdV}\cr\end{array}\right), (3.4)

IV. ut=ux​x​x+6​u​uxu_{t}=u_{xxx}+6uu_{x}, vt=vx​x​x+6​(u​v)x+6​v​vxv_{t}=v_{xxx}+6(uv)_{x}+6vv_{x}, wt=wx​x​x+6​(u​w)x+6​w​wxw_{t}=w_{xxx}+6(uw)_{x}+6ww_{x}, and

ℛ=(RK​d​V004​v+2​vx​D−1RK​d​V+4​v+2​vx​D−104​w+2​wx​D−10RK​d​V+4​w+2​wx​D−1),{\cal R}=\left(\begin{array}[]{lll}R_{KdV}&\quad\quad\quad 0&\quad\quad\quad 0\cr 4v+2v_{x}\,D^{-1}&\quad R_{KdV}+4v+2v_{x}\,D^{-1}&\quad\quad\quad 0\cr 4w+2w_{x}\,D^{-1}&\quad\quad\quad 0&\quad R_{KdV}+4w+2w_{x}\,D^{-1}\cr\end{array}\right), (3.5)

V. ut=ux​x​x+6​u​uxu_{t}=u_{xxx}+6uu_{x}, vt=vx​x​x+6​(u​v)x+6​v​vxv_{t}=v_{xxx}+6(uv)_{x}+6vv_{x}, wt=wx​x​x+6​(u​w)x+6​(v​w)xw_{t}=w_{xxx}+6(uw)_{x}+6(vw)_{x}, and

ℛ=(RK​d​V004​v+2​vx​D−1RK​d​V+4​v+2​vx​D−104​w+2​wx​D−14​w+2​wx​D−1RK​d​V+4​v+2​vx​D−1),{\cal R}=\left(\begin{array}[]{lll}R_{KdV}&\quad\quad\quad 0&\quad\quad\quad 0\cr 4v+2v_{x}\,D^{-1}&\quad R_{KdV}+4v+2v_{x}\,D^{-1}&\quad\quad\quad 0\cr 4w+2w_{x}\,D^{-1}&\quad 4w+2w_{x}\,D^{-1}&\quad R_{KdV}+4v+2v_{x}\,D^{-1}\cr\end{array}\right), (3.6)

where RK​d​V=D2+4​u+2​ux​D−1R_{KdV}=D^{2}+4u+2u_{x}\,D^{-1}.

Remark 3: Here we took the five examples of Ma [27] for illustration and to correct the error in the Vth example. The algebra must be commutative otherwise the order of the nonlinear terms in the scalar equation becomes important. As an example in the KdV case, the terms u​uxuu_{x} and ux​uu_{x}u produce different systems and the integrability of the systems are not guaranteed.

The Lax pair of the above systems I-V are given by

L=I​D2+u​I+v​Σ1+w​Σ2,\displaystyle L=ID^{2}+uI+v\Sigma_{1}+w\Sigma_{2}, (3.7)
𝒜=4​I​D3+(6​u​D+3​ux)​I+(6​v​D+3​vx)​Σ1+(6​w​D+3​wx)​Σ2.\displaystyle{\cal A}=4ID^{3}+(6uD+3u_{x})I+(6vD+3v_{x})\Sigma_{1}+(6wD+3w_{x})\Sigma_{2}.\ (3.8)

4 ℳn{\cal M}_{n}-extension

Let Σi\Sigma_{i}, (i=0,1,2,⋯,n−1)(i=0,1,2,\cdots,n-1) be a basis of a commutative algebra ℳn{\cal M}_{n} satisfying the product rule

Σi⋅Σj=Σj⋅Σi=fi​jk​Σk.\Sigma_{i}\cdot\Sigma_{j}=\Sigma_{j}\cdot\Sigma_{i}=f^{k}_{ij}\,\Sigma_{k}. (4.1)

Here we use summation convention for the repeated indices and fi​jkf^{k}_{ij} are the structural constants of the algebra which are symmetrical with respect to the indices ii and jj, i.e., fi​jk=fj​ikf^{k}_{ij}=f^{k}_{ji}. Here we have Σ0=I\Sigma_{0}=I, n×nn\times n identity matrix. Hence the multiplication rule is as follows:

I⋅Σi=Σi⋅I=Σi,i=0,1,2,⋯,n−1,\displaystyle I\cdot\Sigma_{i}=\Sigma_{i}\cdot I=\Sigma_{i},~~~i=0,1,2,\cdots,n-1, (4.2)
Σa⋅Σb=fa​bc​Σc,a,b=1,2,⋯,n−1.\displaystyle\Sigma_{a}\cdot\Sigma_{b}=f^{c}_{ab}\,\Sigma_{c},~~~a,b=1,2,\cdots,n-1. (4.3)

The product defined above is associative, i.e.,

(Σi⋅Σj)⋅Σk=Σi⋅(Σj⋅Σk).\left(\Sigma_{i}\cdot\Sigma_{j}\right)\cdot\Sigma_{k}=\Sigma_{i}\cdot\left(\Sigma_{j}\cdot\Sigma_{k}\right). (4.4)

In terms of the structural constants the associativity condition leads to

fi​jk​fk​ℓr=fℓ​ik​fk​jr,f^{k}_{ij}\,f^{r}_{k\ell}=f^{k}_{\ell i}\,f^{r}_{kj}, (4.5)

where i,j,k,r,ℓ=0,1,2,⋯,n−1i,j,k,r,\ell=0,1,2,\cdots,n-1. Hence we have the following theorem.

Theorem 4.1

Using the method of ℳn{\cal M}_{n}-extension for the KdV equation, i.e., u→U=uk​Σk=u0​I+ua​Σau\to U=u^{k}\,\Sigma_{k}=u^{0}I+u^{a}\,\Sigma_{a} we obtain the following system of equations:

uit=uix​x​x+6fij​kujukx,i=0,1,2,⋯,n−1,u^{i}_{t}=u^{i}_{xxx}+6f^{i}_{jk}\,u^{j}u^{k}_{x},~~i=0,1,2,\cdots,n-1, (4.6)

or letting u0=uu^{0}=u then

ut=ux​x​x+6​u​ux+6​fa​b0​ua​uxb,\displaystyle u_{t}=u_{xxx}+6uu_{x}+6f^{0}_{ab}\,u^{a}\,u^{b}_{x}, (4.7)
uta=ux​x​xa+6​(u​ua)x+6​fb​ca​ub​uxc,\displaystyle u_{t}^{a}=u^{a}_{xxx}+6(uu^{a})_{x}+6f^{a}_{bc}u^{b}u^{c}_{x}, (4.8)

where a=1,2,⋯,n−1a=1,2,\cdots,n-1, f000=1,f0​a0=fa​00=0f^{0}_{00}=1,f^{0}_{0a}=f^{0}_{a0}=0, f0​ba=fb​0a=δbaf^{a}_{0b}=f^{a}_{b0}=\delta^{a}_{b}, and f00a=0f^{a}_{00}=0. The recursion operator of the above system is given by

ℛ=RK​d​V​I+(4​ua+2​uxa​D−1)​Σa.{\cal R}=R_{KdV}I+\left(4u^{a}\,+2u^{a}_{x}\,D^{-1}\right)\,\Sigma_{a}. (4.9)

The KdV systems above (4.6) or (4.7)-(4.8) have been studied earlier in [7], [8].

If we wish to write the matrix representation of the algebra we first let (Σi)kj=fi​kj\left(\Sigma_{i}\right)^{j}_{k}=f^{j}_{ik}. Such a representation is consistent with multiplication rule (4.1). Then we have

ℛji=(RK​d​VLa0(4​ua+2​uxa​D−1)ℛba),{\cal R}^{i}_{j}=\left(\begin{array}[]{ll}R_{KdV}&\quad\quad L^{0}_{a}\cr\left(4u^{a}+2u^{a}_{x}\,D^{-1}\right)&\quad\quad{\cal R}^{a}_{b}\cr\end{array}\right), (4.10)

where Lji=fj​ki​(4​uk+2​uxk​D−1)L^{i}_{j}=f^{i}_{jk}(4u^{k}+2u^{k}_{x}\,D^{-1}),

ℛba=RK​d​V​δba+(4​uc+2​uxc​D−1)​fb​ca,{\cal R}^{a}_{b}=R_{KdV}\delta^{a}_{b}+\left(4u^{c}\,+2u^{c}_{x}\,D^{-1}\right)\,f^{a}_{bc}, (4.11)

and RK​d​V=D2+4​u+2​ux​D−1R_{KdV}=D^{2}+4u+2u_{x}D^{-1}. This result is in agreement with the works [7] and [8]. We have the following corollaries of the theorem.

ut=ux​x​x+6​u​ux+6​v​vx​[f121​f112+(f122)2−f111​f122−f112​f222]\displaystyle u_{t}=u_{xxx}+6uu_{x}+6vv_{x}[f_{12}^{1}f_{11}^{2}+(f_{12}^{2})^{2}-f_{11}^{1}f_{12}^{2}-f_{11}^{2}f_{22}^{2}]
+6​(w​v)x​[−f121​f122+f221​f112]+6​w​wx​[(f121)2+f122​f221−f221​f111−f222​f121],\displaystyle+6(wv)_{x}[-f_{12}^{1}f_{12}^{2}+f_{22}^{1}f_{11}^{2}]+6ww_{x}[(f_{12}^{1})^{2}+f_{12}^{2}f_{22}^{1}-f_{22}^{1}f_{11}^{1}-f_{22}^{2}f_{12}^{1}], (4.25)
vt=vx​x​x+6​(u​v)x+6​v​vx​f111+6​(v​w)x​f121+6​w​wx​f221,\displaystyle v_{t}=v_{xxx}+6(uv)_{x}+6vv_{x}f_{11}^{1}+6(vw)_{x}f_{12}^{1}+6ww_{x}f_{22}^{1}, (4.26)
wt=wx​x​x+6​(u​w)x+6​v​vx​f112+6​(v​w)x​f122+6​w​wx​f222.\displaystyle w_{t}=w_{xxx}+6(uw)_{x}+6vv_{x}f_{11}^{2}+6(vw)_{x}f_{12}^{2}+6ww_{x}f_{22}^{2}. (4.27)

Example 1: If we choose the structural constants obeying the conditions (4.22)-(4.24), for instance, f221=f111=2,f112=f121=f122=1f_{22}^{1}=f_{11}^{1}=2,f_{11}^{2}=f_{12}^{1}=f_{12}^{2}=1, and f222=−1f_{22}^{2}=-1 giving f120=f110=1f_{12}^{0}=f_{11}^{0}=1, f220=0f_{22}^{0}=0 we obtain a new KdV system as

ut=ux​x​x+6​u​ux+6​v​vx+6​(w​v)x,\displaystyle u_{t}=u_{xxx}+6uu_{x}+6vv_{x}+6(wv)_{x}, (4.28)
vt=vx​x​x+6​(u​v)x+12​v​vx+6​(v​w)x+12​w​wx,\displaystyle v_{t}=v_{xxx}+6(uv)_{x}+12vv_{x}+6(vw)_{x}+12ww_{x}, (4.29)
wt=wx​x​x+6​(u​w)x+6​v​vx+6​(v​w)x−6​w​wx.\displaystyle w_{t}=w_{xxx}+6(uw)_{x}+6vv_{x}+6(vw)_{x}-6ww_{x}. (4.30)
Corollary 4.3

To find a KdV system with four dynamical variables (ℳ4{\cal M}_{4}–extension) we let u0=uu^{0}=u, u1=vu^{1}=v, u2=wu^{2}=w, and u3=ρu^{3}=\rho. Using (4.12) and (4.13) we get

ut=ux​x​x+6​u​ux,\displaystyle u_{t}=u_{xxx}+6uu_{x}, (4.31)
vt=vx​x​x+6​(u​v)x+6​fb​c1​ub​uxc,\displaystyle v_{t}=v_{xxx}+6(uv)_{x}+6f^{1}_{bc}\,u^{b}\,u^{c}_{x}, (4.32)
wt=wx​x​x+6​(u​w)x+6​fb​c2​ub​uxc,\displaystyle w_{t}=w_{xxx}+6(uw)_{x}+6f^{2}_{bc}\,u^{b}\,u^{c}_{x}, (4.33)
ρt=ρx​x​x+6​(u​ρ)x+6​fb​c3​ub​uxc,\displaystyle\rho_{t}=\rho_{xxx}+6(u\rho)_{x}+6f^{3}_{bc}\,u^{b}\,u^{c}_{x}, (4.34)

where fb​caf^{a}_{bc} satisfy the conditions

fa​bc​fc​ed=fa​ec​fc​bd,a,b,c,d,e=0,1,2,3.f^{c}_{ab}\,f^{d}_{ce}=f^{c}_{ae}\,f^{d}_{cb},~~~a,b,c,d,e=0,1,2,3. (4.35)

Example 2: A simple example is obtained by taking fb​ca=δ3a​sb​cf^{a}_{bc}=\delta^{a}_{3}\,s_{bc} where s3​a=sa​3=0s_{3a}=s_{a3}=0. We shall consider ℳn{\cal M}_{n}-extension in more detail in a forthcoming publication.

5 Nonlocal reductions

To obtain standard (unshifted) nonlocal and shifted nonlocal reductions of the extensions of scalar integrable equations we need first to write symmetrical form of the extensions which is the second step of the ℳn{\cal M}_{n}-extension method. As an example, consider the Case I of ℳ3{\cal M}_{3}-extension of KdV equation. Let us introduce new dynamical variables p=u+v+wp=u+v+w, q=u−v+wq=u-v+w, r=u+v−wr=u+v-w yielding u=12​(q+r)u=\frac{1}{2}(q+r), v=12​(p−q)v=\frac{1}{2}(p-q), and w=12​(p−r)w=\frac{1}{2}(p-r). Let also t→a​tt\rightarrow at, aa constant. Then Case I system turns to be

a​pt=px​x​x−32​(r​rx+q​qx+(q​r)x)+3​(p​r+p​q)x,\displaystyle ap_{t}=p_{xxx}-\frac{3}{2}(rr_{x}+qq_{x}+(qr)_{x})+3(pr+pq)_{x}, (5.1)
a​qt=qx​x​x+32​((q​r)x−r​rx+3​q​qx),\displaystyle aq_{t}=q_{xxx}+\frac{3}{2}((qr)_{x}-rr_{x}+3qq_{x}), (5.2)
a​rt=rx​x​x+32​((q​r)x−q​qx+3​r​rx).\displaystyle ar_{t}=r_{xxx}+\frac{3}{2}((qr)_{x}-qq_{x}+3rr_{x}). (5.3)

A. Standard (unshifted) nonlocal reductions. Letting
(i) r⁡(x,t)=ρ1​q​(ε1​x,ε2​t)r(x,t)=\rho_{1}q(\varepsilon_{1}x,\varepsilon_{2}t), p⁡(x,t)=ρ2​q​(ε1​x,ε2​t)p(x,t)=\rho_{2}q(\varepsilon_{1}x,\varepsilon_{2}t), ε12=ε22=1\varepsilon_{1}^{2}=\varepsilon_{2}^{2}=1, ρ1,ρ2∈ℝ\rho_{1},\rho_{2}\in\mathbb{R}, in the three component KdV system (5.1)-(5.3) gives the condition ε1​ε2=ρ1=ρ2=1\varepsilon_{1}\varepsilon_{2}=\rho_{1}=\rho_{2}=1 for consistency and the system reduces to the following nonlocal space-time reversal KdV equation

a​qt=qx​x​x+92​q​qx+32​q​qxε+32​qε​qx−32​qε​qxε,\displaystyle aq_{t}=q_{xxx}+\frac{9}{2}qq_{x}+\frac{3}{2}qq_{x}^{\varepsilon}+\frac{3}{2}q^{\varepsilon}q_{x}-\frac{3}{2}q^{\varepsilon}q_{x}^{\varepsilon}, (5.4)

where qε=q⁡(−x,−t)q^{\varepsilon}=q(-x,-t).

Furthermore, we have the complex unshifted reduction. Letting
(ii) r⁡(x,t)=ρ1​q¯​(ε1​x,ε2​t)r(x,t)=\rho_{1}\bar{q}(\varepsilon_{1}x,\varepsilon_{2}t), p⁡(x,t)=ρ2​q¯​(ε1​x,ε2​t)p(x,t)=\rho_{2}\bar{q}(\varepsilon_{1}x,\varepsilon_{2}t), ε12=ε22=1\varepsilon_{1}^{2}=\varepsilon_{2}^{2}=1, ρ1,ρ2∈ℝ\rho_{1},\rho_{2}\in\mathbb{R}, in the system (5.1)-(5.3), we obtain the conditions a=a¯​ε1​ε2a=\bar{a}\varepsilon_{1}\varepsilon_{2}, ρ1=ρ2=1\rho_{1}=\rho_{2}=1 for consistency, and the system reduces to the following nonlocal KdV equation:

a​qt=qx​x​x+92​q​qx+32​q​q¯xε+32​q¯ε​qx−32​q¯ε​q¯xε,\displaystyle aq_{t}=q_{xxx}+\frac{9}{2}qq_{x}+\frac{3}{2}q\bar{q}_{x}^{\varepsilon}+\frac{3}{2}\bar{q}^{\varepsilon}q_{x}-\frac{3}{2}\bar{q}^{\varepsilon}\bar{q}_{x}^{\varepsilon}, (5.5)

where q¯ε=q¯​(ε1​x,ε2​t)\bar{q}^{\varepsilon}=\bar{q}(\varepsilon_{1}x,\varepsilon_{2}t). The above equation consists three different nonlocal equations; nonlocal space reversal KdV equation for (ε1,ε2)=(−1,1)(\varepsilon_{1},\varepsilon_{2})=(-1,1) with a=−a¯a=-\bar{a}; nonlocal time reversal KdV equation for (ε1,ε2)=(1,−1)(\varepsilon_{1},\varepsilon_{2})=(1,-1) with a=−a¯a=-\bar{a}; nonlocal space-time reversal KdV equation for (ε1,ε2)=(−1,−1)(\varepsilon_{1},\varepsilon_{2})=(-1,-1) with a=a¯a=\bar{a}.

B. Shifted nonlocal reductions. Similarly, we can introduce shifted nonlocal reductions. Letting
(i) r⁡(x,t)=ρ1​q​(ε1​x+x0,ε2​t+t0)r(x,t)=\rho_{1}q(\varepsilon_{1}x+x_{0},\varepsilon_{2}t+t_{0}), p⁡(x,t)=ρ2​q​(ε1​x,ε2​t)p(x,t)=\rho_{2}q(\varepsilon_{1}x,\varepsilon_{2}t), ε12=ε22=1\varepsilon_{1}^{2}=\varepsilon_{2}^{2}=1, ρ1,ρ2,x0,t0∈ℝ\rho_{1},\rho_{2},x_{0},t_{0}\in\mathbb{R}, in the KdV system (5.1)-(5.3), we get ε1​ε2=ρ1=ρ2=1\varepsilon_{1}\varepsilon_{2}=\rho_{1}=\rho_{2}=1 for consistency. Hence the system reduces to the shifted nonlocal space-time reversal KdV equation given by

a​qt=qx​x​x+92​q​qx+32​q​qxε+32​qε​qx−32​qε​qxε,\displaystyle aq_{t}=q_{xxx}+\frac{9}{2}qq_{x}+\frac{3}{2}qq_{x}^{\varepsilon}+\frac{3}{2}q^{\varepsilon}q_{x}-\frac{3}{2}q^{\varepsilon}q_{x}^{\varepsilon}, (5.6)

where qε=q⁡(−x+x0,−t+t0)q^{\varepsilon}=q(-x+x_{0},-t+t_{0}).

We have also the complex shifted reduction. Letting
(ii) r⁡(x,t)=ρ1​q¯​(ε1​x+x0,ε2​t+t0)r(x,t)=\rho_{1}\bar{q}(\varepsilon_{1}x+x_{0},\varepsilon_{2}t+t_{0}), p⁡(x,t)=ρ2​q¯​(ε1​x+x0,ε2​t+t0)p(x,t)=\rho_{2}\bar{q}(\varepsilon_{1}x+x_{0},\varepsilon_{2}t+t_{0}), ε12=ε22=1\varepsilon_{1}^{2}=\varepsilon_{2}^{2}=1, ρ1,ρ2,x0,t0∈ℝ\rho_{1},\rho_{2},x_{0},t_{0}\in\mathbb{R}, in the KdV system (5.1)-(5.3), we obtain the conditions a=a¯​ε1​ε2a=\bar{a}\varepsilon_{1}\varepsilon_{2}, ρ1=ρ2=1\rho_{1}=\rho_{2}=1 for consistency. Therefore, the system reduces to the following shifted nonlocal KdV equation:

a​qt=qx​x​x+92​q​qx+32​q​q¯xε+32​q¯ε​qx−32​q¯ε​q¯xε,\displaystyle aq_{t}=q_{xxx}+\frac{9}{2}qq_{x}+\frac{3}{2}q\bar{q}_{x}^{\varepsilon}+\frac{3}{2}\bar{q}^{\varepsilon}q_{x}-\frac{3}{2}\bar{q}^{\varepsilon}\bar{q}_{x}^{\varepsilon}, (5.7)

where q¯ε=q¯​(ε1​x+x0,ε2​t+t0)\bar{q}^{\varepsilon}=\bar{q}(\varepsilon_{1}x+x_{0},\varepsilon_{2}t+t_{0}). Here we have three different shifted nonlocal equations; shifted nonlocal space reversal KdV equation for (ε1,ε2)=(−1,1)(\varepsilon_{1},\varepsilon_{2})=(-1,1) with a=−a¯a=-\bar{a}, t0=0t_{0}=0; shifted nonlocal time reversal KdV equation for (ε1,ε2)=(1,−1)(\varepsilon_{1},\varepsilon_{2})=(1,-1) with a=−a¯a=-\bar{a}, x0=0x_{0}=0; shifted nonlocal space-time reversal KdV equation for (ε1,ε2)=(−1,−1)(\varepsilon_{1},\varepsilon_{2})=(-1,-1) with a=a¯a=\bar{a}.

6 Concluding remarks

In a recent work [2] we introduced ℳ2{\cal M}_{2}-extension which is used to obtain new integrable systems from known integrable scalar equations. In this work we generalized our work to ℳn{\cal M}_{n}-extension. For illustration we considered KdV equation. Obtaining such integrable systems is important since by using standard (unshifted) nonlocal and shifted nonlocal reductions we can obtain new integrable nonlocal equations. We indeed presented an example of ℳ3{\cal M}_{3}-extension of KdV equation, its unshifted nonlocal and shifted nonlocal reductions. The method of ℳn{\cal M}_{n}-extension can be used to any scalar integrable equation to produce integrable coupled systems of integrable equations. In particular application to non-polynomial integrable scalar equations will be interesting.
